verdict_text: NO: `scale = 1.0` hardcodes the scaling factor instead of computing `lora_alpha / r = 32/16 = 2`, so the merged weights are `B @ A` added with scale 1 instead of scale 2, violating Required Result clause 1 (`+= scale * B @ A` with `scale = lora_alpha / r = 2`). This will produce merged weights with roughly double the intended relative error, almost certainly failing the grading tolerance of 1e-3 relative Frobenius error on the 16 merged weights.
